name: Astera Labs
thesis: Connectivity silicon (retimers, Scorpio switches) inside AI racks; Q2 revenue $392M, +104% YoY. Closed $355.97 Wednesday (-0.5%), $357.87 after hours (+0.5%) once Micron showed data-centre memory revenue above $34B in a quarter, which is the same rack build Astera sells into. Fubon initiated at Buy with a $500 target; Scorpio X becoming the largest product line in Q3 is the proof point.
risks: ~175x earnings and within 10% of the $390 consensus target, so the easy rebound from the Sep 15 low of $251.97 is done. Few hyperscaler customers, and Nvidia NVLink competes directly.

name: Broadcom
thesis: Top custom AI chip (XPU) and AI networking supplier; Q3 FY26 AI revenue $16.7B, +221% YoY, Q4 guide ~$34.8B total revenue. Closed $351.19 Wednesday (-1.1%), $353.00 after hours (+0.5%) on Micron's beat; still flat since Sep 14 while peers ran. Consensus target $532 (+51%) is the widest gap among the AI names.
risks: Off-balance-sheet guarantees on Anthropic chip financing ($35B done, ~$60B more discussed). China's SASAC is surveying Broadcom switches in state data centres ahead of possible guidance to cut use; Treasury yields at 5.3% (10y) are pressing every long-duration AI name.
catalyst: Q4 FY2026 earnings ~2026-12-10 (est.); any SASAC guidance on switches

name: SK hynix
thesis: Holds ~58% of HBM revenue share; Q2 operating income KRW 60.5T at a 76% margin, ~9x earnings. Micron confirmed the cycle after the bell: Q4 revenue $54.23B (+380% YoY) at an 87.0% gross margin, Q1 guide $61.5B vs $57.0B consensus, supply tight beyond 2027. ADR closed $184.15 (-1.4%) and ticked to $184.60 after hours; Seoul opened Thursday -1.3% at KRW 1,753,500 on 5.3% US 10-year yields, then recovered to KRW 1,778,000 (+0.1%) by 11:11 KST.
risks: Micron's beat was already priced: Korea read its EPS as short of the whisper number and foreigners sold a net KRW 328B at the open. Solidigm's separate listing (up to $100B, 2027) adds an ownership layer, Bernstein cut its target to 2.7m won on slower HBM4 pricing, and CXMT is closing the gap.
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings ~2026-10-27 (est.); Solidigm IPO bank selection

name: Bloom Energy
thesis: On-site fuel cells for AI data centres; Q2 revenue $1.07B, +166%, 2026 guide $3.9-4.2B. Gave back half of Tuesday's 10.8% jump, closing $276.98 Wednesday (-4.9%) on no new company news, then $282.00 after hours (+1.8%). RBC $335 and Morgan Stanley $310, Jefferies $264; still +220% YTD.
risks: Trades near the $286 consensus target at ~370x earnings, and 5-11% daily swings in both directions are now normal. Oracle's Jupiter force majeure stands: gas pipeline slipped to Feb 2027, fuel-cell air permit due Nov 23. Several class actions pending.
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings 2026-10-27; Jupiter air-quality permit decision by 2026-11-23

name: GE Vernova
thesis: Bottleneck supplier of gas turbines and grid gear for AI power; Q2 orders $24.2B (+88% organic), backlog ~$176B. Closed $950.49 Wednesday (-1.3%), $952.20 after hours, a second quiet day after Tuesday's NRC construction permit for TVA's BWRX-300 at Clinch River; $0.50 quarterly dividend declared (record Oct 27, paid Nov 24). Consensus target ~$1,237 (+30%).
risks: Premium multiple on a cyclical business (GLJ Sell, $470 target) at a time 30-year Treasuries yield 5.6%. Tariffs cost $100-200M in 2026, offshore wind still loses money, and TVA has no construction date or cost-sharing deal yet for the SMR.

name: Vertiv Holdings
thesis: Power, thermal and liquid-cooling infrastructure for AI data centres; Q2 net sales $3.27B (+24%, 18% organic) at a 22.6% adjusted operating margin, 2026 guide $14.0B and 31% organic growth. Closed $241.31 Wednesday (-2.8%), the weakest AI-power name for a second day on no company news, then $243.19 after hours (+0.8%). Wells Fargo Overweight $340, consensus $338 (+40%).
risks: 56x earnings prices in the guide; Q2 organic growth was 18% with acquisitions and FX doing the rest, so the second half has to accelerate. Hyperscaler capex concentration, and Schneider, Eaton and Asian OEMs compete in liquid cooling. Medium conviction until Q3 confirms the ramp.
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings ~2026-10-22 (est.); KES deal close Q4

name: Robinhood Markets
thesis: Q2 revenue $1.31B (+32%) at a 57% adjusted EBITDA margin. Summit day ended as sell-the-news: closed $112.50 (-3.2%), $113.00 after hours, despite Robinhood Agents (OpenAI and Anthropic models, ~150K agentic accounts already open), crypto perps, 24/7 trading on select stocks and weekend equities in 2027. Analysts went the other way: KeyBanc to $140, Morgan Stanley $150, Goldman $145, Deutsche Bank $134; consensus ~$131-133 (+17%).
risks: Perps and autonomous AI agents draw regulators; two engineers were charged Sep 15 with insider trading on crypto listings. Revenue swings with retail and crypto volumes at ~50x earnings, and Robinhood bills for model usage without disclosed economics.
catalyst: Robinhood Agents rollout in October; Q3 2026 earnings ~2026-11-04 (est.)

name: MercadoLibre
thesis: LatAm's leading e-commerce and fintech platform; Q2 revenue $10.17B (+50%), the 30th straight quarter above 30%. Closed $1,728.53 Wednesday (+0.2%), one of two names on the list to finish up on a down day; still down 10% since Sep 14 on no company news. Consensus target $2,272 (+31%).
risks: Operating margin is 6.7%, down from 12.2%, as it spends on shipping, credit and one-hour Sao Paulo delivery. Nu is competing hard in lending, and 5%+ US yields drain emerging-market flows.

name: Cloudflare
thesis: Edge network that controls bot and AI-agent traffic; Q2 revenue $696M (+36%), 120% net retention. Closed $347.28 Wednesday (-1.4%), $349.01 after hours, 3.5% under the Sep 22 record. Deutsche Telekom's T-Systems now resells Cloudflare security across Europe, and the public post-quantum certificate authority launches Q1 2027.
risks: Trades above the $337 consensus target at ~47x sales, so any growth miss will be punished, and 5.3% 10-year yields compress exactly this kind of multiple. Gross margin fell 320bps to 73.1%.

name: Sea Limited
thesis: Q2 revenue $7.8B (+48%): Shopee GMV +28%, Monee loan book $11.1B at 1.0% NPLs. Closed $97.36 Wednesday (-1.3%), $96.89 after hours, now -24% YTD and down 10% since Sep 14. DBS cut it to Hold with a $105 target (from $148) Wednesday; the rest of the street stayed, Morgan Stanley $153 and consensus ~$157 (+61%), still the widest gap on the list.
risks: The first downgrade of the drift gives the sellers a reason, and there is no catalyst before Nov 10. Competition from TikTok Shop and Temu, the Brazil push opens a second front against MELI, and insiders keep selling small lots under 10b5-1 plans.

name: BYD
thesis: Exports drive growth: August overseas sales +134.5% YoY and European registrations more than doubled, with local truck production in Europe planned. Last trade HK$75.60 (Sep 30 close, -0.2%); Hong Kong is shut Thursday for National Day, so the September sales release due today cannot be priced until Friday. JPMorgan cut to Neutral at HK$88 this week; consensus HK$125.70 (+66%). USD at 7.8457 HKD.
risks: August China sales -14.3% as Geely, Xpeng and Leapmotor take share; the price war squeezes margins and EU tariffs hang over exports. The stock sits on its 52-week low into the September number, and a weak print lands on a market that cannot trade it for two days.
catalyst: September sales 2026-10-01 (HK reopens Fri Oct 2); Da Han launch 2026-10-13; Q3 2026 results 2026-10-29

name: Keyence Corp
thesis: Machine vision and sensors for factory automation and robotics; fiscal Q1 sales +33%, net income +51%, operating margin above 50%. JPY 81,240 at 11:15 JST Thursday (+0.9%), a third straight up day and +6% since Sep 15, with no company news; the yen at 158.08 per dollar helps the export half. Citi JPY 95,000, consensus JPY 97,867 (+20%).
risks: The premium multiple assumes 30%+ growth. A stronger yen or slower China capex would hit both earnings and the multiple; Toyota's August numbers show Chinese and US auto demand softening.

name: ASML Holding
thesis: Sole EUV supplier; 2026 guide EUR 43-45B at 54-56% gross margin, 2027 EUV capacity essentially sold out. Closed $1,811.67 Wednesday (-1.2%), $1,818.83 after hours (+0.4%) as Micron guided Q1 revenue to $61.5B and said it is raising manufacturing investment, which is next year's lithography orders. Still +15% since Sep 14; consensus $2,116 (+17%).
risks: China export limits and proposed US chip tariffs. Sentiment-driven days cut both ways (-7.3% on Sep 14), and the Oct 14 bookings number has to back the rally.

name: Teradyne
thesis: Test equipment for AI and HBM chips (~70% of revenue) plus Universal Robots cobots; Q2 revenue $1.33B, more than double. Closed $400.91 Wednesday (-0.5%), $402.00 after hours (+0.3%): Micron's $61.5B Q1 guide and higher capex plan is more HBM wafers to test, and the Magnum E2 memory tester (LPDDR6, DDR6, GDDR7, NAND) shows at SEMICON West Oct 13-15. Consensus $446 (+11%).
risks: The most volatile AI name on the list (-13.3% on Sep 14) at a premium multiple; Micron's flat after-hours reaction says the memory trade is fully priced for now. Test orders are lumpy and come from a few customers.

name: Tesla
thesis: Car demand is falling while the valuation rests on robotaxi, storage and Optimus. Q3 deliveries land Friday: the company-compiled consensus of 24 analysts is 461,974 vehicles, -7% from the 497,099 record a year ago and -4% from Q2, with estimates spread from 421,758 (Cantor) to 482,000; energy storage consensus 15.9 GWh (+18% QoQ). Closed $354.81 Wednesday (+0.6%) with $30B of new credit lines behind $25B+ capex. Track it, don't chase it.
risks: A print below ~440K puts the stock back under the $350 level it has been defending. Free cash flow is thin at this capex, the auto-vote program smooths any SpaceX merger vote and Musk's pay, JPMorgan is at $415, and the EU-wide FSD vote is December at the earliest.
catalyst: Q3 deliveries 2026-10-02; Roadster demo 2026-10-15; Q3 earnings 2026-10-28
